earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only wordlists (Somerville & Weigall 1896; Tryon & Hackman 1983); no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Dalle Ceste, Carlo. 2024. Dynamics of change in person-number indexes in insular Western Oceanic. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Vangunu stress. p.74: 'Although Marovo and Vangunu have no grammatical description, aspects of the former are given in Evans (2008a; 2008b; 2009), while the latter is sketched out in Bourchier (2007).' Cites the unpublished 'Bourchier, Louise. 2007. Vangunu report. Australian National University' (examples quoted from its pp. 9-16) -- the only description of Vangunu grammar on record.

sources.citation: Frostad, Benedicte Haraldstad. 2012. A grammar of Ughele. PhD, LOT/Radboud. (mentions of Vangunu/Bareke)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Vangunu and Bareke only as members of the eastern New Georgia subgroup; no phonological data on them.

sources.citation: Davis, Karen. 2003. A grammar of the Hoava language, Western Solomons. Pacific Linguistics 535. (ch.1 survey of earlier New Georgia sources)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Lynch, Ross & Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic Languages. Curzon. p.22
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a naming remark: Bareke/Bariki/Mbareke/Mbariki is a dialect of the Vangunu language; no data.

sources.citation: Tryon, D.T. & B.D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72. Canberra: ANU. (viii+490 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Vangunu (no. 29) and Mbareke (no. 28) appear in wordlists and POc sound-correspondence tables only; p.57 n.1 'Phonemic transcription unless otherwise noted throughout' (no stress marks); vowel table p.105: Mbareke/Vangunu *o > o,u with fn.25 about POc *mpoe 'pig' only; p.31 notes the two communities regard Mbareke and Vangunu as not mutually intelligible.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1926. A comparative study of the Melanesian Island languages. Cambridge University Press (New Georgia chapter).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.7.25)
sources.note: Ray's New Georgia section gives short phonological notes per language and may comment on accent for the Marovo/Mbareke material he received from Somerville & Weigall; only controlled-lending copy on archive.org (comparativestudy0000rays).

sources.citation: Somerville, B.T. 1897. Ethnographical notes in New Georgia, Solomon Islands. Journal of the Anthropological Institute 26: 357-412.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; ethnographic notes, native words are in the Marovo ('Eastern') dialect; mentions Vangunu/Mbariki districts only; vocabulary was handed to S.H. Ray.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Vangunu language'; Glottolog 5.x vang1243 page; ELAR search 'Vangunu'/'Marovo'; ANU Open Research searches 'Vangunu'/'Bareke'/'Marovo grammar'
sources.note: No phonology anywhere; ELAR hits are Chambers' Kubokota materials that merely mention Vangunu; ANU repository has no Vangunu description besides the items above.
